domain: Religious Authority / Commitment Systems / Political Theology
topic_summary: Analysis of the 1890 Manifesto reversing Mormon polygamy practice under US federal coercion. The kernel is the divine-command substrate grounding marriage legitimacy. Two readings emerge: continuationist (polygamy remains doctrinally valid, suspended for prudential reasons) vs substitutionist (monogamy now doctrinally required, polygamy rescinded). The reversal occurred via exogenous federal pressure rather than endogenous theological revision, creating an M-set gap where the authority structure absorbed coercion without surfacing it as legitimate grounds for doctrinal change.

key_entities: LDS Church leadership (prophetic authority claiming direct divine revelation)
US Federal Government (territorial sovereignty enforcer via Edmunds-Tucker Act)
key_tensions: Divine command vs federal law (theological authority vs territorial sovereignty)
Doctrinal immutability vs institutional survival (kernel fixity vs pragmatic adaptation)
Prophetic authority vs coercion visibility (revelation claim vs exogenous pressure acknowledgment)

fracture_scan.notes: No fractures detected. Kernel contest is genuine: three readings emit structurally different constraints (different victim sets, different beneficiary structures, different epsilon values). Continuationist reading treats polygamy as suspended but valid (high epsilon suppression of alternatives). Substitutionist reading treats polygamy as rescinded (moderate epsilon via excommunication). Coercion visibility reading surfaces exogenous override as mountain (very low epsilon — historical record). All three readings share the divine_marriage_command kernel but instantiate different constraints from it.
